module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1036

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1036](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1036)
- [AlHa91] Alon, N. and Hajnal, A., *Ramsey graphs contain many distinct induced subgraphs*.
  Graphs Combin. (1991), 1-6.
- [ErHa89b] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., *On the number of distinct induced subgraphs of a graph*.
  Discrete Math. (1989), 145-154.
- [Sh98] Shelah, Saharon, *Erdős and Rényi conjecture*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1998), 179-185.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos1036

/--
`G` contains at least `k` many induced subgraphs which are not pairwise isomorphic, that is,
there is a family of at least `k` many sets of vertices whose induced subgraphs are pairwise
non-isomorphic.
-/
def HasManyNonIsomorphicInducedSubgraphs {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ 𝒮 : Set (Set V), (𝒮.Pairwise fun s t => IsEmpty (G.induce s ≃g G.induce t)) ∧
    k ≤ (𝒮.ncard : ℝ)

/--
Neither `G` nor its complement contains a balanced complete bipartite graph $K_{k,k}$ on more
than `m` vertices as a (not necessarily induced) subgraph. That is, there are no two disjoint
sets of `k` vertices with $2k > m$ such that every pair of vertices from different sets is
adjacent in `G`, or every such pair is non-adjacent in `G`.
-/
def NoLargeBiclique {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (m : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ k : ℕ, ((completeBipartiteGraph (Fin k) (Fin k)).IsContained G ∨
    (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin k) (Fin k)).IsContained Gᶜ) → (2 * k : ℝ) ≤ m

/--
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices which does not contain a trivial (empty or complete) graph on
more than $c\log n$ vertices. Must $G$ contain at least $2^{\Omega_c(n)}$ many induced subgraphs
which are not pairwise isomorphic?

This is true, and was proved by Shelah [Sh98].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1036.lean"]
theorem erdos_1036 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (G.cliqueNum : ℝ) ≤ c * Real.log (n : ℝ) → (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ c * Real.log (n : ℝ) →
        HasManyNonIsomorphicInducedSubgraphs G ((2 : ℝ) ^ (δ * (n : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

/--
Alon and Hajnal [AlHa91] proved that $G$ must contain at least
$$\exp\left(n(\log n)^{-O(\log\log n)}\right)$$
many non-isomorphic induced subgraphs.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1036.variants.alon_hajnal :
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (G.cliqueNum : ℝ) ≤ c * Real.log (n : ℝ) → (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ c * Real.log (n : ℝ) →
        HasManyNonIsomorphicInducedSubgraphs G
          (Real.exp ((n : ℝ) * Real.log (n : ℝ) ^ (-(C * Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)))))) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa89b] proved that if neither $G$ nor its complement contains a balanced
complete bipartite graph $K_{k,k}$ on more than $c\log n$ vertices (as a not necessarily induced
subgraph) then $G$ contains at least $2^{\Omega_c(n)}$ many non-isomorphic induced subgraphs.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1036.variants.erdos_hajnal :
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      NoLargeBiclique G (c * Real.log (n : ℝ)) →
        HasManyNonIsomorphicInducedSubgraphs G ((2 : ℝ) ^ (δ * (n : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1036

reformulations.difference: The sources count isomorphism classes of induced subgraphs; Lean instead asks for a sufficiently large family of vertex subsets inducing pairwise non-isomorphic graphs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For finite vertex types, any such family injects into the quotient of vertex subsets by induced-graph isomorphism. Conversely, choosing one representative of every quotient class gives a pairwise non-isomorphic family with exactly the quotient's cardinality. Thus the definition is equivalent to the source's cardinality lower bound. Proved as Review1036.many_iff_quotient_count in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

reformulations.difference: Shelah states the hypothesis using the maximum homogeneous-set size, a strict inequality, and log base 2. Lean uses separate non-strict bounds on clique and independence numbers and the natural logarithm.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The two separate bounds are equivalent to bounding their maximum. Since log₂ n = log n / log 2 and the statement quantifies over every positive c, changing logarithm base just reparametrizes c. Strict and non-strict thresholds are equivalent for this uniformly quantified asymptotic claim: one direction weakens a strict inequality, and the other applies the strict version with an enlarged constant for n ≥ 2. The counting conclusion is equivalent by the representative-family lemma. Proved as Review1036.main_equivalence without using the reviewed theorem.

reformulations.difference: The primary literature parametrizes a balanced biclique by the size k of one part; Lean's NoLargeBiclique bounds its total number of vertices, 2k.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: NoLargeBiclique G (2*m) is exactly the condition that every balanced biclique in G or its complement has part size at most m. Because the qualitative exponential statement quantifies over all positive c, the factor of two is absorbed by reparametrizing c. Strict forbidden-threshold conventions are likewise absorbed by enlarging c for sufficiently large n. These equivalences, including the quotient-count conclusion, were proved as Review1036.biclique_source_equivalence in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

sources_consulted: Shelah, S., Erdős and Rényi conjecture, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 82 (1998), 179–185; introduction, notation, definition of I(G), and main theorem. LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/9707226

Alon, N. and Hajnal, A., Ramsey graphs contain many distinct induced subgraphs, Graphs and Combinatorics 7 (1991), 1–6; introduction and Theorem 1.1. https://www.cs.tau.ac.il/~nogaa/PDFS/Publications/Ramsey%20graphs%20contain%20many%20distinct%20induced%20subgraphs.pdf

Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., On the number of distinct induced subgraphs of a graph, Discrete Math. 75 (1989), 145–154; Definition 3, graph conventions, and Section 2, Theorem 2. https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1989-24.pdf

review.notes: Both definitions and all three theorems were checked. Alon–Hajnal's Theorem 1.1 gives the stated exp(n(log n)^(-C log log n)) bound when the maximum homogeneous-set size is O_c(log n). The primary papers support all three solved tags and the affirmative answer. Independent Lean checks covered n=0, n=1, k=0, empty/singleton vertex types, the 2^n counting upper bound, and non-induced K_{2,2} containment in a complete graph. The test and equivalence lemmas compiled with only standard axioms. The erdosproblems.com page was Cloudflare-blocked, so verification used the cited primary literature instead. The linked formal-proof statement matches after the verified reformulations and its source contains no explicit sorry or custom axioms. Full kernel verification in its specified Lean/Mathlib 4.29.1 environment was not completed; replay with the sandbox's 4.33.1 produced compatibility errors, which are not evidence of an incorrect proof record.
